question: Why did the error rate go up on 20 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The error rate increase is likely due to a configuration change in the service.
why_chain: The error rate increased after a deployment to ap-south, which is a configuration change.
The deployment to ap-south happened 34 minutes after the error rate increase, which is right time and place.
The error rate in the eu-west region, where the service is located, increased after the deployment to ap-south.

evidence.summary: Error rate for service checkout in region eu-west rose from 0.52% to 1.08% (+109%), with a change point at 2026-03-20T02:40:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service checkout in region eu-west: 1 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.09).
At the same time, request volume for service checkout in region eu-west stayed about the same (289 per 5 min before, 312 per 5 min after, +8%).
At the same time, p95 latency for service checkout in region eu-west stayed about the same (219 ms before, 222 ms after, +1%).
Deployed auth v4.12 to ap-south (routine release) (auth, ap-south; 146 min before the change; record R005; fit: different service/region, so unlikely to be the cause)
Deployed catalog v8.27 to ap-south (catalog, ap-south; 34 min after the change; record R006; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)

reasons: ✗ The closest change event is 146 min before the change, too far to be convincing.
✗ It concerns a different service/region than the one that changed.
✗ No logs or alerts from the affected segment confirm the problem.
✓ Request volume stayed steady, ruling out a traffic spike.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.
